chunks.title: CLO Official Website Basic Tutorial — Making a Shirt
chunks.content: ## CLO Official Website Basic Tutorial — Making a Shirt This document provides a step-by-step tutorial on using the CLO official website and software to create a digital shirt. It covers key processes such as pattern design, fabric selection, sewing simulation, and 3D garment visualization using CLO’s tools. ### Introduction to CLO and Its Interface This section explains the basics of CLO, a 3D garment visualization software widely used in fashion design and virtual prototyping. It introduces the main interface elements relevant to creating a shirt. - CLO enables digital garment creation through 2D pattern design and 3D simulation. - The workspace includes a 2D pattern window and a 3D garment window for simultaneous editing and visualization. - Important tool panels include the Property Editor for adjusting fabric and pattern properties, and the Object Browser for managing garment parts. ### Creating a Shirt Pattern This section covers how to create the fundamental shirt pattern pieces within CLO, including technical details about pattern drafting and adjustments. - Start by drafting the basic shirt pattern pieces such as front and back bodice, sleeves, collar, and cuffs. - Use the polygon and curve tools to draw the outlines of each pattern piece. - Specify measurements precisely to ensure proper fit; CLO supports metric and imperial units. - Utilize internal lines and points to mark sewing lines, grainlines, and darts. - Apply symmetry options to mirror pattern pieces when applicable, reducing manual work. - Patterns can be imported from external DXF or AI files or created natively within CLO. ### Fabric Selection and Property Adjustment This section explains how to select and configure fabric properties to simulate realistic drape and behavior on the garment. - CLO allows importing or choosing from a library of fabrics with predefined physical properties. - Adjust parameters such as stretch, thickness, weight, and friction to match real fabric behavior. - Fabric texture and color can be set by importing images or using preset materials. - Proper fabric simulation is crucial for realistic garment fitting and movement during animation. ### Sewing and Assembly Simulation This section details how to digitally sew the pattern pieces together and preview the assembled shirt on a 3D avatar. - Use the sewing tool to define stitch lines between corresponding edges of pattern pieces. - CLO supports various sewing types including segment sewing (edge to edge) and free sewing (point to point). - Confirm sewing lines by checking the 3D garment window to ensure pieces join correctly without distortion. - The software simulates fabric collision and gravity, allowing real-time observation of how the shirt fits and hangs on the avatar. - Adjust seam allowances and sewing tension parameters to fine-tune the garment assembly. ### 3D Garment Visualization and Final Adjustments This section focuses on using CLO’s 3D simulation to review the shirt design and make necessary refinements. - The 3D window displays the shirt on a customizable avatar, allowing rotation, zoom, and pose changes.
